learningObjectives: Identify the default control types and theme configuration options for Pega UI elements.
Configure dynamic attributes (Visible, Disabled, Required) on UI elements using conditions and When Rules.

elements.description: The source lists Autocomplete, Check boxes, Drop-down lists, Links, Rich-text editors and Text input. This is an illustrative list, not proof that every unlisted control is unsupported or requires custom development.
Themes style UI elements consistently across the application. The source illustrates the Pegasus theme. Visibility, disabling and required-value behavior use separate dynamic configuration.

elements.text: A form can reveal vehicle details after a user selects vehicle ownership, or require a phone number for text contact. Dynamic rules adapt the presentation; this improves responsiveness without promising that every interaction avoids a page refresh.

elements.description: Designing UI elements to adapt according to user choices. Provides:
items: Fewer full-page refreshes for improved responsiveness

elements.description: Controls whether a UI element is shown:
items: Source table: Always, Custom Condition, When Rule, If not blank, If not zero.

elements.description: Disabled prevents interaction with the configured field. This UI behavior does not replace server-side authorization or data integrity checks.
items: Options: Never | Always (always read-only) | Custom Condition | When Rule

elements.description: Controls whether a field must be filled before the form submits:
items: Options: Never | Always | Custom Condition (required when expression is true) | When Rule
The source lists If not blank and If not zero under Visible, not under Required or Disabled.

elements.description: Two ways to configure conditional display in Dynamic UI:
items: CUSTOM CONDITION — for SHORT, one-off expressions (e.g., check one dropdown value)
WHEN RULE — for COMPLEX or REUSABLE conditions shared across multiple UI elements

elements.term: 'If not blank' and 'If not zero' — Visible ONLY
elements.description: 'If not blank' shows an element only when the field value is not blank. 'If not zero' shows when the value is not zero. These options appear ONLY under the Visible attribute — not under Disabled or Required.

examPitfalls.title: Know the three defaults: Visible=Always, Disabled=Never, Required=Never
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Questions ask candidates to fill in the default setting for the Disabled or Required attribute. Candidates guess 'Always' for all three, not knowing only Visible defaults to Always while both Disabled and Required default to Never.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Visible defaults to Always (elements show by default). Disabled defaults to Never (elements are editable by default). Required defaults to Never (fields are optional by default).

examPitfalls.title: Custom Condition = short one-off; When Rule = complex or reusable
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Questions describe a visibility condition and ask whether to use a Custom Condition or a When Rule. Candidates always choose Custom Condition. Use Custom Condition for simple, one-time expressions; use a When Rule when the logic is complex, reused in multiple places, or needs to be tested independently.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Custom Condition is for short, simple expressions. When Rule is for complex conditions intended for reuse across multiple forms.

examPitfalls.title: 'If not blank' and 'If not zero' are Visible-only — not for Disabled or Required
examPitfalls.trapDescription: A question asks which conditions are available for the Required attribute. Candidates select 'If not blank' — unaware this built-in condition exists only in the Visible attribute's drop-down and is absent from Disabled and Required.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: 'If not blank' and 'If not zero' are ONLY available as Visible options. They do not appear under Disabled or Required.

examPitfalls.title: Themes = styling only — not behavior
examPitfalls.trapDescription: A scenario asks which feature controls field visibility. Candidates select Theme because themes affect the UI — but themes handle only colors and fonts, never behavioral conditions like Visible, Disabled, or Required.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Themes configure the APPEARANCE of UI elements (buttons, links, headers). Dynamic attributes (Visible, Disabled, Required) control element behavior. These are separate concerns.

examPitfalls.title: Dynamic UI reduces full-page refreshes — not eliminates them
examPitfalls.trapDescription: An exam statement says dynamic UI 'eliminates all full-page refreshes.' Candidates mark it correct because they associate dynamic UI with a smoother experience. The correct claim is 'reduces' — not 'eliminates.'
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Dynamic UI REDUCES full-page refreshes, improving responsiveness. It does not eliminate all page refreshes.

examPitfalls.title: Listed controls are examples, not an exhaustive support matrix
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Absence from the six-item source list does not mean a control is unsupported or needs custom development.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Remember the source’s examples; verify supported controls in the relevant field and UI configuration.

examPitfalls.title: Custom Condition and When Rule are available for ALL 3 dynamic attributes
examPitfalls.trapDescription: A question asks which condition options apply to the Required attribute. Candidates select only 'Custom Condition,' missing that When Rule is also available for all three attributes — Visible, Disabled, and Required.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Custom Condition and When Rule are available for ALL THREE attributes: Visible, Disabled, and Required.

optionExplanations.B: Never is not the stated default.
optionExplanations.D: A named condition is not the unconditional default.

practiceQuiz.scenario: What is the default disabled setting for UI elements in Pega Platform?
practiceQuiz.hint: Separate styling from conditional behavior and identify the setting described in this View.

optionExplanations.B: Always would prevent interaction in the configured View.
optionExplanations.C: An inline condition is a configured alternative.
optionExplanations.D: A named When Rule is a configured alternative.

practiceQuiz.scenario: You have a complex visibility condition that will be reused across multiple forms. Which visibility setting should you use?
practiceQuiz.hint: Separate styling from conditional behavior and identify the setting described in this View.
practiceQuiz.rationale: A reusable When Rule centralizes this logic.

optionExplanations.A: A reusable When Rule centralizes this logic.
optionExplanations.B: A one-off expression is less suitable for the stated reuse.
optionExplanations.C: Nonblank checks do not express the complex condition.
optionExplanations.D: Always would discard the conditional requirement.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A confirmation View displays an optional next appointment date selected earlier. Which built-in visibility option hides this display when its date is empty?
practiceQuiz.hint: Separate styling from conditional behavior and identify the setting described in this View.
practiceQuiz.rationale: If not blank tests whether the already selected date exists.

optionExplanations.A: If not blank tests whether the already selected date exists.
optionExplanations.B: An expression can implement it, but the built-in shortcut is requested.
optionExplanations.C: A reusable rule can implement it, but is not the direct shortcut.
optionExplanations.D: Nonzero is not the source’s optional-date example.

practiceQuiz.scenario: After account creation, a confirmation View should always prevent editing the stored Account Type. Which Disabled setting fits this View?
practiceQuiz.hint: Separate styling from conditional behavior and identify the setting described in this View.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Always prevents editing in this confirmation View.

optionExplanations.A: Always prevents editing in this confirmation View.
optionExplanations.B: Never would not disable the field.
optionExplanations.C: No conditional expression is needed for the stated always-disabled View.
optionExplanations.D: No named conditional rule is needed for this unconditional setting.

options.text: Reduced visual clutter on the screen
Automatic field validation without When Rules

practiceQuiz.hint: Separate styling from conditional behavior and identify the setting described in this View.

optionExplanations.A: Responsive adaptation is a listed benefit.
optionExplanations.C: The source describes fewer full-page refreshes.
optionExplanations.D: Dynamic UI does not replace configured validation.

practiceQuiz.hint: Separate styling from conditional behavior and identify the setting described in this View.

optionExplanations.A: Reuse across forms favors a named When Rule.
optionExplanations.B: Nonblank does not evaluate the stated age condition.
optionExplanations.C: Always ignores the conditional display requirement.
optionExplanations.D: Nonzero does not evaluate the stated age threshold.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A 'Mobile number' field must be required only when the user selects 'Text' as their preferred contact method. This is a simple, form-specific condition. Which required setting should you use?
practiceQuiz.hint: Separate styling from conditional behavior and identify the setting described in this View.
practiceQuiz.rationale: A short form-specific expression fits Custom Condition.

optionExplanations.A: A short form-specific expression fits Custom Condition.
optionExplanations.B: Always would require the number for other contact methods too.
optionExplanations.C: Never would make the number optional for text contact.
optionExplanations.D: The source does not list this under Required.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Which pair of conditional settings does the source list for Visible, Disabled and Required?

options.text: If not blank and If not zero
When Rule and If not blank

practiceQuiz.scenario: What is the default Required setting for UI elements, and what does it mean?

options.text: Never — users can proceed without entering a value
Always — users must enter a value to proceed
Custom Condition — required only when a condition is met
When Rule — required based on a configurable When Rule

practiceQuiz.hint: Separate styling from conditional behavior and identify the setting described in this View.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Never means optional under this Required setting.

optionExplanations.A: Never means optional under this Required setting.
optionExplanations.B: Always is an alternative, not the default.
optionExplanations.C: Custom Condition is an alternative to the default.
optionExplanations.D: When Rule is also a configured alternative.

practiceQuiz.scenario: An SA is configuring dynamic attributes on a Claims form in Pega Constellation. Which TWO dynamic attributes can be applied to a UI element using a When Rule or condition?

options.text: Visible — controls whether the element is shown or hidden based on a condition evaluated at runtime
Disabled — controls whether the element is interactive (editable) or read-only based on a condition
Font-size — dynamically adjusts the text size of the element based on user role or screen size
Z-Index — controls the visual stacking order of overlapping elements at runtime based on urgency

practiceQuiz.hint: Separate styling from conditional behavior and identify the setting described in this View.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Visible can evaluate conditional display. Disabled can evaluate conditional interaction.

optionExplanations.C: Font size is not one of these three dynamic attributes.
optionExplanations.D: Z-index is not one of these named configuration attributes.

practiceQuiz.scenario: An SA is designing a Claims form where the 'Injury Description' field should only appear when the claim type is 'Personal Injury.' Which TWO elements are needed to implement this conditional visibility?

options.text: A When Rule or condition expression that evaluates whether the claim type equals 'Personal Injury'
The Visible attribute on Injury Description, linked to the selected condition or When Rule
A Decision Table that changes the field's background color to transparent when the condition is false
A separate View for each claim type to avoid using conditional visibility configuration

practiceQuiz.hint: Separate styling from conditional behavior and identify the setting described in this View.
practiceQuiz.rationale: The logic evaluates the selected claim type. Linking Visible to that logic controls display.

optionExplanations.A: The logic evaluates the selected claim type.
optionExplanations.B: Linking Visible to that logic controls display.
optionExplanations.C: Transparent color is not the requested visibility configuration.
optionExplanations.D: Separate Views are not required for this conditional-field pattern.

quickRecap.value: Autocomplete, Check boxes, Drop-down lists, Links, Rich-text editors, Text input. Not an exhaustive support matrix.
Themes provide consistent UI styling; Pegasus is the illustrated theme. Dynamic configuration governs element behavior.
Real-time response, reduced visual clutter, fewer full-page refreshes.
Visible = Always. Disabled = Never. Required = Never.
'If not blank' and 'If not zero' — only for Visible attribute, NOT available for Disabled or Required.
Custom Condition = short one-off expressions. When Rule = complex or reusable conditions.
Custom Condition and When Rule are available for Visible, Disabled, AND Required.
